title: RevMed’s pancreatic cancer drug first - Nature Biotechnology
gist: The FDA approved Revolution Medicines' RAS inhibitor Rasonque (daraxonrasib) in August for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, with early lung-cancer data following in September. It binds the active GTP-bound RAS via a cyclophilin A molecular glue mechanism, unlike KRAS G12C inhibitors.

insights.claim: The FDA approved Revolution Medicines' Rasonque (daraxonrasib) in August as a first-in-class RAS inhibitor for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, the most common form of pancreatic cancer.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: First RAS-targeted approval in pancreatic cancer is a major validation of a long-undruggable target.
insights.quote: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in August approved Revolution Medicines’ drug
insights.locator: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

insights.claim: An early-stage trial in September showed Rasonque has promise in lung cancer, bolstering hopes RAS inhibitors could treat pancreatic, lung and colorectal tumors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Label expansion into lung and colorectal would multiply the addressable market; early data are not yet proof.
insights.quote: These results bolster hopes that RAS inhibitors such as Rasonque could help combat a variety of hard-to-treat cancers

insights.claim: Rasonque blocks multiple forms of RAS, including mutated KRAS and other RAS proteins present in over 90% of pancreatic tumors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Broad RAS coverage targets a much larger pancreatic population than mutation-specific drugs.
insights.quote: Rasonque blocks multiple forms of the RAS protein

insights.claim: Unlike KRAS G12C inhibitors Lumakras and Krazati, which bind the 'off' state, Rasonque binds the GTP-bound 'on' conformation of RAS that drives oncogenic signaling.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Targeting the active state is a different competitive approach than G12C drugs and may reach beyond G12C-mutant tumors.
insights.quote: Rasonque binds the RAS GTPase in its GTP-bound ‘on’ conformation that drives oncogenic signaling

insights.claim: Rasonque works as a molecular glue, binding both the abundant cellular protein cyclophilin A and RAS to prevent RAS interacting with its signaling partners.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The molecular-glue mechanism is a template for drugging other hard targets via abundant chaperone proteins.
insights.quote: The drug works through a molecular glue mechanism, binding to both the abundant cellular protein cyclophilin A and RAS
